lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. In two hours, she will run the eight hundred metres at Sports Day.
**Kavya:** I did not sign up for this. My PE teacher signed me up for this.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about something much, much smaller.
**Narrator:** Inside her thigh are millions of muscle cells. And inside each cell are hundreds of tiny power stations.
**Narrator:** This is one of them.
**Mitch:** Hi. Mitch. **Mitochondrion**.
**Mitch:** And yes, before you say it. I am 'the powerhouse of the cell'.
**Mitch:** I know. Everyone knows. It's the only thing anyone remembers from Year 7. It's on a mug.
**Mitch:** I have the mug.
**Narrator:** Mitch's family has been in the energy business for about two billion years.
**Mitch:** Never had a day off. Not one. Not even on my birthday. I don't know when my birthday is.
**Narrator:** The Powerhouse. Episode one: Sports Day.
**Narrator:** Nine a.m. Kavya's breakfast has been digested. A delivery arrives, by blood.
**Gloria:** Hiii! Gloria! **Glucose**! I'm a sugar! From the toast! I'm basically a snack with feelings!
**Mitch:** Gloria is glucose. She's the fuel. She's... a lot.
**Gloria:** I've got SO much energy stored in me, Mitch. In my chemical bonds! Want to see?
**Mitch:** Not yet. First I need oxygen.
**Otto:** Did somebody say...
**Oscar:** ...oxygen?
**Otto:** I'm Otto.
**Oscar:** I'm Oscar. We're oxygen. We always travel as a pair.
**Otto:** O two. It's a whole thing.
**Mitch:** The twins come in from the lungs, through the blood. They finish each other's sentences. It's exhausting.
**Narrator:** When glucose meets oxygen inside a mitochondrion, we get **aerobic respiration**. Aerobic means **with oxygen**.
**Mitch:** **Glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water**. And energy is **released**.
**Gloria:** Ooh, it's like a dance where everybody swaps partners!
**Mitch:** It's a chemical reaction, Gloria. But... yes. Fine. The atoms swap partners.
**Carl:** And then... there's me. Carl. **Carbon dioxide**. The waste product.
**Carl:** Nobody throws a party when I arrive. They throw me OUT. Into the blood, to the lungs, and out of her mouth.
**Carl:** Every time Kavya breathes out, that's me being thrown out. Rude.
**Mitch:** And that's **water**. Wally. Wally doesn't talk.
**Narrator:** Scientists write the same reaction as a **symbol equation**.
**Mitch:** **C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O**
**Otto:** Six pairs of us? That's twelve oxygen atoms!
**Oscar:** Plus six inside Gloria. That's eighteen!
**Otto:** And eighteen on the other side!
**Mitch:** No atoms are made, and none are destroyed. Same atoms, new partners. That's why the equation **balances**.
**Gloria:** So you basically MAKE energy out of me!
**Mitch:** No.
**Mitch:** Energy can't be made, Gloria. It was already stored in you. I **release** it.
**Mitch:** Write 'respiration **releases** energy'. If you write 'makes energy', an examiner somewhere quietly cries into their tea.
**Narrator:** So where does all that released energy go?
**Mitch:** Let's look at this morning's requests.
**Mitch:** Muscles. Want energy to **move**. Always. Muscles never stop asking.
**Mitch:** **Growth and repair**. Building new cells, and making big molecules like proteins.
**Mitch:** And **keeping warm**. Thirty-seven degrees. All day. Every day.
**Kavya:** It's thirty-four degrees OUTSIDE. Why are you keeping me WARM?
**Mitch:** Because you're a **mammal**, Kavya. Mammals and birds keep a steady body temperature. Not my rule. I just pay the bill.
**Narrator:** Cells that need a lot of energy, like muscle cells, are packed with mitochondria.
**Mitch:** This muscle cell has about two thousand of us. Two thousand Mitches.
**Mitch:** There's a Mitch in accounts I really don't like.
**Narrator:** Inside each mitochondrion, the inner membrane is **folded**. That gives a large surface area for the reactions.
**Mitch:** We fold it, like a tiny, sad accordion. More folds, more room to work.
**Narrator:** Now. A very common mistake.
**Kavya:** Respiration is just breathing, right? Like the respiratory system?
**Mitch:** No.
**Mitch:** **Breathing** is your lungs moving air in and out, using muscles and your ribs. That's the delivery van.
**Mitch:** **Respiration** is a **chemical reaction** inside every living cell. That's me. I'm the factory.
**Otto:** Breathing brings us in...
**Oscar:** ...respiration uses us up.
**Carl:** And breathing out gets rid of me. As usual.
**Narrator:** Fish respire. Bacteria respire. And plants respire.
**Fern:** Hiii, Mitch!
**Mitch:** Fern.
**Fern:** We plant cells respire **all the time**, day and night. Photosynthesis only happens when it's light.
**Fern:** So we do both! We're the day shift AND the night shift!
**Mitch:** Fern works in a pot plant on a windowsill. Fern has never once complained. I find that suspicious.
**Narrator:** Photosynthesis **stores** energy in glucose. Respiration **releases** it. They're roughly opposites.
**Narrator:** Eleven a.m. The eight hundred metres.
**Kavya:** Okay. Okay. I can do this. It's just two laps. Two... long... laps.
**Narrator:** The race starts. Suddenly, Kavya's leg muscles need far more energy, far more quickly.
**Mitch:** All hands! Gloria! Twins! I need oxygen, NOW!
**Otto:** Coming! Her heart's beating faster!
**Oscar:** She's breathing faster and deeper!
**Otto:** But we just can't get here fast enough!
**Mitch:** No oxygen, no aerobic respiration. I'm going to have to call... him.
**Narrator:** When there isn't enough oxygen, muscle cells switch to **anaerobic respiration**. Anaerobic means **without oxygen**.
**Larry:** HELLOOO! Larry! **Lactic acid**! Who ordered emergency energy?!
**Mitch:** Larry is what happens when you skip the oxygen. He's not evil. He's just... the cheap option.
**Larry:** **Glucose → lactic acid**. No oxygen needed! Super speedy!
**Gloria:** Wait. You're only using a tiny bit of my energy?
**Larry:** I'm in a hurry! You're only partly broken down, so you release **much less energy**.
**Mitch:** Much less energy. But it's fast, and it keeps her running.
**Kavya:** Why... do my legs... feel like they're on FIRE?
**Larry:** That's me! Lactic acid builds up and makes your muscles tired and achy. It's called **muscle fatigue**!
**Larry:** You're welcome!
**Narrator:** Kavya crosses the line.
**Kavya:** I came fourth. Out of five. I'm lying down now. This is my life now.
**Narrator:** Kavya has stopped running. So why is she still panting?
**Kavya:** I. Stopped. Running. Why. Am I. Still. Breathing like this?
**Mitch:** Because Larry left a mess. And you owe us oxygen.
**Otto:** We're here now!
**Oscar:** Where's the lactic acid?
**Narrator:** The extra oxygen needed to break down the lactic acid is called the **oxygen debt**. That's why you keep breathing hard after exercise.
**Mitch:** You borrowed energy without oxygen. Now you pay it back, with oxygen.
**Mitch:** Even your cells have bills, Kavya.
**Larry:** This isn't goodbye! I'll be back at the next PE lesson!
**Mitch:** So. **Aerobic**: needs oxygen, releases **lots** of energy. **Anaerobic**: no oxygen, **a little** energy, and Larry.
**Narrator:** Meanwhile, at the bakery across the road, a very different relative is hard at work.
**Bao:** Hello. I'm Bao. I'm a **yeast**. A single-celled **fungus**. Yes, a fungus. Don't make that face.
**Bao:** When I run out of oxygen, I don't make lactic acid like Larry. I do **fermentation**.
**Bao:** **Glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide**. And a little energy.
**Carl:** Wait. Carbon dioxide? Me?
**Bao:** You, Carl. Your bubbles make the bread dough **rise**. You make it soft and fluffy.
**Carl:** Someone... wants me?
**Carl:** I'm going to cry. I can't cry. I'm a gas.
**Bao:** The **ethanol** evaporates when the bread is baked. Adults also use fermentation to make wine and beer. We will not be discussing that. Kavya is twelve.
**Mitch:** Bao is my cousin. Technically. Very technically. We both respire. Bao makes bread. I make sore legs.
**Narrator:** You can even catch Carl in the act. Bubble carbon dioxide through **limewater**, and it turns **milky**.
**Carl:** It's my one party trick. Clear to cloudy. I've been practising for years.

chapters.title: The cast saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the cast would like to save you some marks.
**Mitch:** One. Respiration is **not** breathing. Breathing moves air. Respiration is a reaction in your cells.
**Gloria:** Two! Energy is **released**, never made! It was in me all along!
**Fern:** Three. Plants respire **all the time**. Day and night. Not just at night!
**Larry:** Four! Anaerobic respiration in muscles makes **lactic acid**. NOT ethanol! That's Bao's thing!
**Otto:** Five. Aerobic releases...
**Oscar:** ...MUCH more energy than anaerobic.
**Carl:** Six. Anaerobic respiration in your muscles doesn't make any carbon dioxide at all.
**Carl:** Story of my life.
**Narrator:** The Powerhouse will return.
**Mitch:** Wally. Anything you'd like to add?
**Wally:** ...Hi.
**Mitch:** He's been saving that for two billion years.
